content.title: Definition of RIP
content.text: transitive verb 1 a : to tear or split apart or open ripped the fabric in half ripped the page while turning it b : to remove quickly or violently ripped the poster off the wall c : to saw or split (wood) with the grain 2 : to slash or slit with or as if with a sharp blade 3 : to hit sharply ripped a double to left field 4 : to utter violently : spit out 5 : criticize, disparage The opposition ripped the president's handling of the issue. The movie was ripped to shreds/pieces by critics. intransitive verb 1 : to become ripped : rend The coat ripped when it got caught on the doorknob. 2 : to go or move very quickly fire ripped through the forest 1 : a rent made by ripping : tear 1 : a body of water made rough by the meeting of opposing tides, currents, or winds 2 : a current of water roughened by passing over an irregular bottom 1 [Latin requiescat in pace] may he rest in peace, may she rest in peace 2 [Latin requiescant in pace] may they rest in peace Synonyms of rip Choose the Right Synonym for rip rip implies a pulling apart in one rapid uninterrupted motion often along a line or joint. ripped the shirt on a nail rend implies very violent or ruthless severing or sundering. an angry mob rent the prisoner's clothes split implies a cutting or breaking apart in a continuous, straight, and usually lengthwise direction or in the direction of grain or layers. cleave implies very forceful splitting or cutting with a blow. a bolt of lightning cleaved the giant oak rive occurs most often in figurative use. a political party riven by conflict Examples of rip in a Sentence Verb She ripped the fabric in half. He ripped open the package. The dog ripped the pillow to shreds. Recent Examples on the Web Examples are automatically compiled from online sources to show current usage.
